01 / SYSTEM

One factory.
Six connected zones.

Open diagram ↗
Simulation environment

NVIDIA Isaac Sim

The 80 × 60 m factory and its task scenes were assembled in NVIDIA Isaac Sim—an OpenUSD-based robotics simulation framework with physically based environments, robot and sensor models, and synthetic-data generation. It provides the controllable geometry, physics, viewpoints, and robot states used for the factory observations on this page.

Official Isaac Sim page ↗

02 / REASONING

Human intent.
Model calls. Physical action.

Model call + physical feedback loop

One instruction stays connected to the factory state from perception to execution.

01 / Human Factory worker Natural-language task
02 / Observe Factory input RGB · robot state · scene
03 / Gemini API Gemini Robotics ER 2 Ground · reason · assign
04 / Interface Executable work plan Task · pose · robot · constraint
05 / World model DreamZero Predict · plan · control
06 / Physical world Robot + factory Act · observe · report
↺

Closed loop. New camera frames, robot states, success signals, and failures return to both model layers. A changed factory event can trigger a fresh VLM call and a new physically grounded plan.

WFactory workerTask description

“Move to the blue bin, pick up the red package, turn around, walk to the conveyor belt, and place the package down.”

Embodied reasoning trace01 / Mobile manipulation
VLM
Gemini Robotics ER 2Google DeepMind VLM · Gemini API
Visual grounding + Tree of Thoughts

The VLM combines the worker’s instruction with the factory image. It identifies the humanoid, blue bin, red target package, and roller conveyor, establishes world frame W, explores alternative pickup routes and grasp poses, then selects the feasible task branch.

robot [0.1, 2.4, 0.0]target [-0.9, 1.1, 0.45]place [1.6, 1.0, 0.65]
WM
DreamZeroNVIDIA · World Action Model
Predictive rollout + embodied control

DreamZero receives the structured work plan rather than the raw sentence. It predicts action-conditioned future states for this humanoid, checks the bin rim, reachability, collision risk, and grasp continuity, then converts the selected subgoals into low-level predictive actions.

  1. 01Walk to bin standbyWalkTo
  2. 02Pre-grasp 0.65 → grasp 0.45 → lift 0.70 mArmGrasp
  3. 03Carry to conveyor standby [1.1, 1.0, 0.0]WalkTo
  4. 04Lower, release at z 0.68, retract armsArmPlace
R
Robot policyExecution response

The robot executes, then reports its pose, gripper state, object state, and a new factory frame. A failed grasp or displaced package re-enters the loop for VLM replanning and another world-model rollout.

Closed-loop executionnavigate → grasp → observe → carry → place → verify
WFactory workerTask description

“Left Robot, pick up the cardboard box and carry it to the handover area. Right Robot, turn around and receive it. Transfer the box safely between both robots.”

Embodied reasoning trace02 / Multi-robot coordination
VLM
Gemini Robotics ER 2Google DeepMind VLM · Gemini API
Grounding + role assignment

The VLM reads the worker’s two-robot instruction and the factory image together. It grounds Robot A, Robot B, the cardboard box, both tables, and the shared handover region, then compares alternative role assignments and chooses one reachable transfer pose.

box [-1.2, 1.8, 0.85]A standby [-0.2, 1.1, 0.0]handover [0.0, 1.1, 0.95]
WM
DreamZeroNVIDIA · World Action Model
Multi-robot predictive execution

DreamZero rolls out both bodies in parallel, evaluates approach clearance, arm reach, payload stability, and timing, and preserves a synchronization barrier: Robot A cannot release until Robot B’s predicted and observed grip states agree.

  1. 01Robot A walks to Table 1, grasps and lifts the boxA / pickup
  2. 02Robot B turns and moves to [0.2, 1.1, 0.0]B / align
  3. 03Both arms converge at the shared handover poseA + B
  4. 04B closes gripper; A releases only after confirmationsync barrier
R
Robot teamExecution response

Both robots execute their assigned branches and stream pose, force, and gripper feedback. If alignment drifts, the world model pauses the release and the VLM regenerates the coordination branch from the updated factory state.

Feedback synchronizedB: close → sense → confirm → A: open → verify
WFactory workerTask description

“Sort every target item on the main conveyor. Arm 1 should pick first; if it misses an item or is busy, Arm 2 must catch it. Place sorted items on the side conveyors.”

Embodied reasoning trace03 / Fail-safe sorting
VLM
Gemini Robotics ER 2Google DeepMind VLM · Gemini API
Scene understanding + task allocation

The VLM grounds two fixed arms, one continuous feed line, incoming parcels, and both side-conveyor destinations. It interprets “Arm 1 first, Arm 2 if missed” as a shared target track with primary and fallback ownership.

arm 1 [0.0, 0.0, 0.4]arm 2 [0.0, 1.2, 0.4]flow +Y / line X = 0.6
WM
DreamZeroNVIDIA · World Action Model
Future-state prediction + fallback control

DreamZero predicts each parcel’s motion and both arms’ reachable futures. Arm 1 receives the first intercept; if grip confirmation is absent before the object leaves its workspace, the predicted target pose and priority transfer to Arm 2.

  1. 01Scan and estimate the target trajectorymonitor
  2. 02Arm 1 intercepts at [0.6, 0.0, 0.15]primary
  3. 03On miss, Arm 2 intercepts at [0.6, 1.2, 0.15]fallback
  4. 04Place at each arm’s dedicated side-conveyor zonesort
R
Robot cellsExecution response

The cells execute while conveyor observations continuously update the shared target track. A miss, blockage, or workload change is returned as a factory event, causing the VLM to revise allocation and DreamZero to roll out the new action branch.

Adaptive loop activeobserve → predict → primary/fallback → verify → update

03 / DATA & ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS

Built with shared
physical AI resources.

We thank NVIDIA for Isaac Sim and the four Physical AI datasets that support factory construction, spatial understanding, predictive world modeling, asset composition, and multi-camera tracking.

01 / Spatial intelligence

PhysicalAI Spatial Intelligence Warehouse

Synthetic warehouse RGB-D observations with object masks and questions for grounding, left–right relations, counting, and metric distance reasoning.

02 / World modeling

PhysicalAI SDG-Warehouse

Isaac Sim warehouse video with synchronized viewpoints and RGB, depth, segmentation, edges, bounding boxes, and camera metadata for physical-AI world modeling.

03 / Factory assets

PhysicalAI SimReady Warehouse 01

A catalog of 753 Isaac Sim-compatible OpenUSD warehouse assets, including racks, pallets, containers, forklifts, and physically graspable objects.

04 / Smart spaces

PhysicalAI Smart Spaces

Time-synchronized indoor scenes with calibration and tracking annotations for people, forklifts, pallet trucks, AMRs, and humanoid robots across multiple cameras.
